name: Kizamani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.note: Only Decker & Abraham 2022 SIL sociolinguistic profile exists; no phonological description located

sources.citation: Decker, Ken & Benard Abraham. 2022. A Sociolinguistic Profile of the Rishiwa and Kizamani (Shuwa-Zamani [ksa]) Languages of Kaduna State, Nigeria. Journal of Language Survey Reports 2022-024. Dallas: SIL International. 53 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 8.3 'Phonetic inventories' (pp. 19-20) gives consonant/vowel tables only; Appendix E note (p. 34): 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' The Kizamani 222-item wordlist is tone-marked (e.g. 'river' kùmɑ́nɑ̀, 'stone' kɑ̄tɑ̄ɾī) but tone is not analysed; 'stress'/'accent'/'prosody' occur nowhere. downloaded via the Internet Archive (live sil.org PDF is behind an automated-access block).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2022. Change Request 2022-024: split [ksa] Shuwa-Zamani into [rsw] Rishiwa and [izm] Kizamani (adopted 2023-01-20). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing; lexicostatistic split rationale only. Sources section names only Decker et al. (forthcoming = Decker & Abraham 2022).

sources.citation: Longdi Sylvanus (SIL Nigeria). 2022. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Kizamani [izm] (form 2022-024_izm).
sources.note: Nothing. Names: autonym Kizamani, alternate Kuzamani, ethnic group Azaman(i), ~2,000 speakers. The 'Knowledge from published sources (dictionaries, grammars)' field is left empty.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-67. DOI 10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210
sources.note: Nothing about Kizamani: Table 1 (pp. 48-49) lists 'Shuwa-Zamani ?' with no vitality and no source; sec. 3.1 phonology covers eBoze only; the word 'stress' occurs nowhere.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2019. An Atlas of Nigerian Languages, ed. IV. Cambridge: Kay Williamson Educational Foundation.
sources.note: Nothing. Entry 422 'Shuwa-Zamani' (p. 90): Kaduna State, Saminaka LGA; Kauru subgroup; 'Source(s) Blench (1986)'; no Refs line at all, i.e. no wordlist, grammar or phonology cited.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2018. Nominal affixing in the Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. In J. R. Watters (ed.), East Benue-Congo: Nouns, pronouns, and verbs, 59-106. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Nothing; Shuwa-Zamani appears only in the classification tree (p. 83). downloaded to only (no Kizamani content worth keeping).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger & Stuart McGill. 2012. The Kainji languages of northwestern and central Nigeria. Circulation draft, 369 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about Shuwa-Zamani (classification list only). Tone sections treat Cinda and Hungwəryə (two level tones H/L, downstep); 'stress' = 0 hits.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2004. The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research. Ms. (Hamburg), 12 pp.
sources.note: Nothing about Shuwa-Zamani; it appears only in the Kauru classification list (App. 1). Phonology section is on eBoze; 'accent' hits are tone-diacritic names only.

sources.citation: Any SIL Nigeria / NBTT phonology statement or orthography guide for Kizamani or Rishiwa (none published as of the 2022 ISO request, whose 'published sources' field is empty).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The 2022 survey notes NBTT-supported Bible translation work in Rishiwa; a phonology statement would normally accompany it and might be the first place a prosody/stress remark for the Kauru group appears. No such document could be found; listed so the gap is explicit.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 1986. [Unpublished field notes / wordlist on Shuwa-Zamani], cited as 'Source(s) Blench (1986)' in Blench 2019, Atlas of Nigerian Languages ed. IV, entry 422.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: The only pre-2021 primary data on the language named anywhere; unpublished and never listed on rogerblench.info (the Internet Archive's index of the whole Kainji directory has no Shuwa-Zamani/Kauru file). Would at most be a tone-marked wordlist; unlikely to state a stress rule.

sources.citation: Shimizu, Kiyoshi. 1982. Ten more wordlists with analyses from the Northern Jos group of Plateau languages. Afrika und Übersee 65(1): 97-134.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Only published tone-marked material from the Kauru/Lere area with 'analyses'; covers Si/Gana/Takaya (Lere cluster), which Blench's Atlas conflates with 'Kuzamani/Rishuwa' but Decker & Abraham 2022 argue is a different language. Relevant only for the identity question, not for Kizamani stress.
